```{r}
#| label: dashboard-setup
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)

data_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1]
if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-control
#| include: false
# Change this value and re-render to show a different income group.
# Options: "Low Income (<1.3)", "Middle Income", "High Income (>3.5)"
available_income_groups <- sort(unique(na.omit(nhanes$IncomeGroup)))
selected_income <- "Low Income (<1.3)"

if (!selected_income %in% available_income_groups) {
  selected_income <- available_income_groups[1]
}

selected_income
```

## The question

Has average BMI among adults age 20-80 in one income group gone up, gone down, or stayed about the same across NHANES survey cycles from 1999-2000 to 2021-2023? The board can use this to decide whether a follow-up analysis is worth asking for.

**Income group shown: `r selected_income`.** Versions for the other income groups (`r paste(setdiff(available_income_groups, selected_income), collapse = " and ")`) can be made on request.

## Trend

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-plot-data
dashboard_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80,
    IncomeGroup == selected_income,
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(Cycle)
  ) |>
  group_by(Cycle) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-plot
ggplot(dashboard_summary, aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "#2f6f73") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, color = "#2f6f73") +
  labs(
    title = paste("Mean BMI for", selected_income),
    subtitle = "Adults age 20-80 in the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom dataset",
    x = "NHANES cycle",
    y = "Mean BMI",
    caption = paste(
      "Each point is the average BMI of adults age 20-80 in this income group, from the classroom NHANES file.",
      "Income group uses the family income-to-poverty ratio: low is under 1.3, high is over 3.5.",
      "People missing BMI or income group are left out. This file has no 2019-2020 cycle.",
      "Unweighted and descriptive: not a U.S. population estimate, and it does not show that income causes BMI.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
```

## Numbers behind the chart

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-summary
kable(
  dashboard_summary,
  col.names = c("NHANES cycle", "Adults (n)", "Mean BMI")
)
```

## What this shows

In this dataset, mean BMI for the `r selected_income` group was `r first(dashboard_summary$mean_bmi)` in `r first(dashboard_summary$Cycle)` and `r last(dashboard_summary$mean_bmi)` in `r last(dashboard_summary$Cycle)`. Each cycle includes at least `r format(min(dashboard_summary$n), big.mark = ",")` adults. This is a description of the pattern over time, not an explanation of why it happened. It can help the board decide what to ask next, for example whether the same pattern shows up in the other income groups.

## Limitation

These are unweighted, descriptive averages from a classroom copy of NHANES. They do not account for the NHANES survey design, do not estimate BMI for U.S. adults, and do not show that income causes BMI.

## Data and privacy

Data come from a cached classroom snapshot (`nhanes_equity_v6`) prepared from CDC/NCHS public-use NHANES files. The dashboard shows group averages only, never individual records.
